blocks.content: When you know your progress is safe, you work differently.
You're more willing to try new ideas. You're not as worried about breaking something, because you can always return to a version that worked.

Without that safety, people often start saving different versions of the same project just to feel secure. You might end up with files like project, project_v2, project_final, project_final_REAL, project_final_REAL_v2, and still not be sure which one actually works.

blocks.alt: File explorer showing a folder with files named project, project_v2, project_final, project_final_REAL, project_final_REAL_v2

blocks.content: At that point, every change feels a bit risky. You hesitate, avoid touching working code, and spend more time being careful than actually improving things.
Git removes that pressure. It lets you move forward with confidence, knowing that nothing you've done is truly lost.
